questions.question: You have been provided with three test tubes. One of them contains distilled water and the other two contain an acidic solution and a basic solution, respectively. If you are given only red litmus paper, how will you identify the contents of each test tube?
answer_steps: Dip the red litmus paper in each test tube. The solution that turns it blue is the base.
Dip this blue litmus paper in the other two. The one that turns it red again is the acid.
The remaining test tube, which changes neither colour, contains distilled water.

questions.question: Why should curd and sour substances not be kept in brass and copper vessels?
answer_steps: Curd and sour substances contain acids.
The acids react with copper and brass to form poisonous compounds that spoil the food.

questions.question: Which gas is usually liberated when an acid reacts with a metal? Illustrate with an example. How will you test for the presence of this gas?
answer_steps: Hydrogen gas is liberated.
Example: $\mathrm{Zn(s) + H_{2}SO_{4}(aq) \rightarrow ZnSO_{4}(aq) + H_{2}(g)}$
Bring a burning candle near the gas: it burns with a pop sound.

questions.question: Metal compound A reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid to produce effervescence. The gas evolved extinguishes a burning candle. Write a balanced chemical equation for the reaction if one of the compounds formed is calcium chloride.
answer_steps: The gas is carbon dioxide and A is calcium carbonate.
$\mathrm{CaCO_{3} + 2HCl \rightarrow CaCl_{2} + H_{2}O + CO_{2}}$

questions.question: Why do HCl, HNO₃, etc., show acidic characters in aqueous solutions while solutions of compounds like alcohol and glucose do not show acidic character?
answer_steps: HCl and HNO₃ give hydrogen ions (H⁺, as H₃O⁺) in water.
Alcohol and glucose contain hydrogen but do not release H⁺ ions in water, so they are not acidic.

questions.question: Why does an aqueous solution of an acid conduct electricity?
answer_steps: An acid in water gives ions: $\mathrm{HCl + H_{2}O \rightarrow H_{3}O^{+} + Cl^{-}}$
These moving ions carry the electric current.

questions.question: Why does dry HCl gas not change the colour of the dry litmus paper?
answer_steps: HCl shows acidic behaviour only when it gives H⁺ ions, and that needs water.
Dry HCl and dry litmus have no water, so no H⁺ ions form and the colour does not change.

questions.question: While diluting an acid, why is it recommended that the acid should be added to water and not water to the acid?
answer_steps: Mixing a concentrated acid with water is highly exothermic.
If water is added to the acid, the heat can make the mixture boil and splash out, and the glass can break; adding acid slowly to water keeps it safe.

questions.question: How is the concentration of hydronium ions (H₃O⁺) affected when a solution of an acid is diluted?
answer_steps: On dilution the same ions are spread through a larger volume.
So the concentration of H₃O⁺ ions per unit volume decreases.

questions.question: How is the concentration of hydroxide ions (OH⁻) affected when excess base is dissolved in a solution of sodium hydroxide?
answer_steps: More base gives more OH⁻ ions in the same volume.
So the concentration of OH⁻ ions increases (up to a limit).

questions.question: You have two solutions, A and B. The pH of solution A is 6 and pH of solution B is 8. Which solution has more hydrogen ion concentration? Which of this is acidic and which one is basic?
answer_steps: A has more hydrogen ion concentration (lower pH).
A is acidic (pH less than 7) and B is basic (pH more than 7).

questions.question: What effect does the concentration of H⁺(aq) ions have on the nature of the solution?
answer_steps: The higher the concentration of H⁺ ions, the lower the pH and the more acidic the solution.
A lower H⁺ concentration makes the solution less acidic or basic.

questions.question: Do basic solutions also have H⁺(aq) ions? If yes, then why are these basic?
answer_steps: Yes, basic solutions also have some H⁺ ions.
They are basic because the concentration of OH⁻ ions is greater than that of H⁺ ions.

questions.question: Under what soil condition do you think a farmer would treat the soil of his fields with quick lime (calcium oxide) or slaked lime (calcium hydroxide) or chalk (calcium carbonate)?
answer_steps: When the soil is too acidic.
These are bases (or a carbonate) and neutralise the extra acid, bringing the pH to a level suitable for crops.

questions.question: What is the common name of the compound $\mathrm{Ca(ClO)_{2}}$?
questions.explanation: Ca(ClO)₂ (calcium hypochlorite) is how bleaching powder is represented.

questions.question: Name the substance which on treatment with chlorine yields bleaching powder.
questions.explanation: Chlorine reacts with dry slaked lime, Ca(OH)₂: $\mathrm{2Ca(OH)_{2} + 2Cl_{2} \rightarrow Ca(ClO)_{2} + CaCl_{2} + 2H_{2}O}$
option_feedback: Quicklime is CaO; chlorine is passed over slaked lime, Ca(OH)₂.

questions.question: Name the sodium compound which is used for softening hard water.
questions.explanation: Washing soda (Na₂CO₃·10H₂O) removes permanent hardness.
option_feedback: Common salt does not soften water.
It is not used for softening water.
Baking soda is used in cooking.

questions.question: What will happen if a solution of sodium hydrocarbonate is heated? Give the equation of the reaction involved.
answer_steps: It decomposes into sodium carbonate, water and carbon dioxide gas.
$\mathrm{2NaHCO_{3} \xrightarrow{\Delta} Na_{2}CO_{3} + H_{2}O + CO_{2}}$

questions.question: Write an equation to show the reaction between Plaster of Paris and water.
answer_steps: $\mathrm{CaSO_{4} \cdot \tfrac{1}{2}H_{2}O + 1\tfrac{1}{2}H_{2}O \rightarrow CaSO_{4} \cdot 2H_{2}O}$
Plaster of Paris sets into a hard solid mass of gypsum.

questions.question: A solution turns red litmus blue, its pH is likely to be
questions.explanation: Turning red litmus blue means the solution is basic, so its pH is above 7.
option_feedback: pH 1 is strongly acidic; it would turn blue litmus red.

questions.question: A solution reacts with crushed egg-shells to give a gas that turns lime-water milky. The solution contains
questions.explanation: Egg-shells are calcium carbonate; an acid releases carbon dioxide from them.
option_feedback: A salt does not release carbon dioxide from egg-shells.
A salt does not release carbon dioxide from egg-shells.
A salt does not release carbon dioxide from egg-shells.

questions.question: 10 mL of a solution of NaOH is found to be completely neutralised by 8 mL of a given solution of HCl. If we take 20 mL of the same solution of NaOH, the amount of HCl solution (the same solution as before) required to neutralise it will be
questions.explanation: Twice the base needs twice the acid: $2 \times 8 = 16$ mL.
option_feedback: Twice the base needs more acid, not less.
That is for 10 mL of NaOH.

questions.question: Which one of the following types of medicines is used for treating indigestion?
questions.explanation: An antacid is a mild base that neutralises the extra acid in the stomach.

questions.question:
Write word equations and then balanced equations for the reaction taking place when –

(a) dilute sulphuric acid reacts with zinc granules.

(b) dilute hydrochloric acid reacts with magnesium ribbon.

(c) dilute sulphuric acid reacts with aluminium powder.

(d) dilute hydrochloric acid reacts with iron filings.
answer_steps: (a) Zinc + sulphuric acid → zinc sulphate + hydrogen: $\mathrm{Zn(s) + H_{2}SO_{4}(aq) \rightarrow ZnSO_{4}(aq) + H_{2}(g)}$
(b) Magnesium + hydrochloric acid → magnesium chloride + hydrogen: $\mathrm{Mg(s) + 2HCl(aq) \rightarrow MgCl_{2}(aq) + H_{2}(g)}$
(c) Aluminium + sulphuric acid → aluminium sulphate + hydrogen: $\mathrm{2Al(s) + 3H_{2}SO_{4}(aq) \rightarrow Al_{2}(SO_{4})_{3}(aq) + 3H_{2}(g)}$
(d) Iron + hydrochloric acid → iron(II) chloride + hydrogen: $\mathrm{Fe(s) + 2HCl(aq) \rightarrow FeCl_{2}(aq) + H_{2}(g)}$

questions.question: Compounds such as alcohols and glucose also contain hydrogen but are not categorised as acids. Describe an Activity to prove it.
answer_steps: Fix two nails on a cork in a beaker and connect them through a bulb and a 6 V battery.
Pour dilute HCl into the beaker: the bulb glows. Repeat with glucose solution and with alcohol: the bulb does not glow.
So acids give ions (H⁺) that conduct electricity, while glucose and alcohol do not give H⁺ ions; they are not acids.

questions.question: Why does distilled water not conduct electricity, whereas rain water does?
answer_steps: Distilled water has almost no ions.
Rain water dissolves gases such as carbon dioxide and other substances from the air, which form ions, so it conducts electricity.

questions.question: Why do acids not show acidic behaviour in the absence of water?
answer_steps: Acidic behaviour is due to H⁺ ions.
Acids release H⁺ ions only in water; without water there are no H⁺ ions.

questions.question:
Five solutions A, B, C, D and E when tested with universal indicator showed pH as 4, 1, 11, 7 and 9, respectively. Which solution is

(a) neutral?

(b) strongly alkaline?

(c) strongly acidic?

(d) weakly acidic?

(e) weakly alkaline?

Arrange the pH in increasing order of hydrogen-ion concentration.
answer_steps: (a) D (pH 7) (b) C (pH 11) (c) B (pH 1)
(d) A (pH 4) (e) E (pH 9)
Increasing H⁺ concentration: C (11) < E (9) < D (7) < A (4) < B (1).

questions.question: Equal lengths of magnesium ribbons are taken in test tubes A and B. Hydrochloric acid (HCl) is added to test tube A, while acetic acid (CH₃COOH) is added to test tube B. Amount and concentration taken for both the acids are same. In which test tube will the fizzing occur more vigorously and why?
answer_steps: In test tube A.
HCl is a strong acid and gives many more H⁺ ions than acetic acid, a weak acid, so hydrogen forms faster.

questions.question: Fresh milk has a pH of 6. How do you think the pH will change as it turns into curd? Explain your answer.
answer_steps: The pH will decrease (go below 6).
Curd contains lactic acid, so the milk becomes more acidic as it sets.

questions.question:
A milkman adds a very small amount of baking soda to fresh milk.

(a) Why does he shift the pH of the fresh milk from 6 to slightly alkaline?

(b) Why does this milk take a long time to set as curd?
answer_steps: (a) Slightly alkaline milk does not turn sour quickly, so it stays fresh for longer.
(b) The lactic acid formed must first neutralise the baking soda before the milk can become acidic and set.

questions.question: Plaster of Paris should be stored in a moisture-proof container. Explain why?
answer_steps: Plaster of Paris reacts with water (moisture) and sets into hard gypsum:
$\mathrm{CaSO_{4} \cdot \tfrac{1}{2}H_{2}O + 1\tfrac{1}{2}H_{2}O \rightarrow CaSO_{4} \cdot 2H_{2}O}$

questions.question: What is a neutralisation reaction? Give two examples.
answer_steps: The reaction of an acid with a base to give a salt and water is neutralisation.
Example: $\mathrm{NaOH(aq) + HCl(aq) \rightarrow NaCl(aq) + H_{2}O(l)}$
Example: $\mathrm{Mg(OH)_{2} + 2HCl \rightarrow MgCl_{2} + 2H_{2}O}$ (an antacid in the stomach)

questions.question: Give two important uses of washing soda and baking soda.
answer_steps: Washing soda: in glass, soap and paper industries; for removing permanent hardness of water; as a cleaning agent.
Baking soda: in baking powder for making cakes and bread soft; as an antacid; in soda-acid fire extinguishers.

questions.question: Methyl orange is added to dilute hydrochloric acid and to aqueous sodium hydroxide. What is the colour of the methyl orange in each solution?
options: Orange in the acid, red in the base
Red in the acid, yellow in the base
Red in the acid, orange in the base
Yellow in the acid, red in the base
questions.explanation: Methyl orange is red in acids and yellow in bases.
option_feedback: Methyl orange is red in acid.
In a base it turns yellow.
The colours are the other way round.

questions.question: Which of the following substances when dissolved in equal volume of water, will have the highest pH value?
questions.explanation: Sodium hydroxide is a strong base: it gives the most OH⁻ ions and the highest pH. Magnesium hydroxide is a weak base.
option_feedback: An acid has a low pH.
An acid has a low pH.
It is a weak base and only slightly soluble.

questions.question: When excess of carbon dioxide is passed through lime water, the milkiness disappears because
options: water soluble calcium carbonate converts to water soluble calcium bicarbonate.
insoluble calcium carbonate converts to water soluble calcium bicarbonate.
water soluble calcium carbonate converts to insoluble calcium bicarbonate.
insoluble calcium carbonate converts to insoluble calcium bicarbonate.
questions.explanation: $\mathrm{CaCO_{3}(s) + H_{2}O(l) + CO_{2}(g) \rightarrow Ca(HCO_{3})_{2}(aq)}$
option_feedback: Calcium carbonate is insoluble: that is why lime water turns milky.
It is the other way round.
Calcium bicarbonate is soluble, so the milkiness goes.

questions.question:
Sara took 2 mL of dilute NaOH solution in a test tube and added two drops of phenolphthalein solution. The solution turned pink. She added dilute H₂SO₄ drop by drop until the solution became colourless. Then she repeated the activity: 2 mL of NaOH needed 20 drops of acid, 3 mL needed 30 drops and 4 mL needed 40 drops.

A. If Sara used concentrated H₂SO₄ in place of dilute H₂SO₄, will the number of drops needed be 40, less than 40 or more than 40 (for 4 mL of NaOH)? Justify your answer. (1)

B. Sara measured 20 drops of dilute H₂SO₄ and found its volume to be 1 mL. If she observed the change in colour by using 3 mL of H₂SO₄, how many mL of NaOH did she take? OR Sara takes 10 drops of dilute H₂SO₄ with two drops of phenolphthalein and adds NaOH dropwise. What change in colour would she observe after 20 drops of NaOH, and why? (2)

C. Write a balanced chemical equation for the reaction. Is it (a) neutralisation and double displacement, (b) neutralisation and precipitation, (c) precipitation and double displacement, or (d) all three? (1)
answer_steps: A. Less than 40: concentrated acid gives more H⁺ ions per drop.

B. 3 mL = 60 drops, and each 10 drops neutralise 1 mL of NaOH, so she took 6 mL of NaOH. OR The colour changes from colourless to pink: once all the acid is neutralised, the solution becomes basic and phenolphthalein turns pink.
C. $\mathrm{2NaOH(aq) + H_{2}SO_{4}(aq) \rightarrow Na_{2}SO_{4}(aq) + 2H_{2}O(l)}$: (a) neutralisation and double displacement. It is not precipitation, because sodium sulphate is soluble.

questions.question: Which of the following is a synthetic indicator?
questions.explanation: Phenolphthalein is made in the laboratory; litmus, turmeric and onion are natural.
option_feedback: Onion is a natural olfactory indicator.

questions.question: Which of the following is an olfactory indicator?
questions.explanation: The smell of vanilla essence disappears in a base, so it is an olfactory (smell) indicator.

questions.question: Explain the manufacture of bleaching powder with chemical reactions. Write any two uses of bleaching powder.
answer_steps: Chlorine from the chlor-alkali process ($\mathrm{2NaCl(aq) + 2H_{2}O(l) \rightarrow 2NaOH(aq) + Cl_{2}(g) + H_{2}(g)}$) is passed over dry slaked lime.
$\mathrm{2Ca(OH)_{2} + 2Cl_{2} \rightarrow Ca(ClO)_{2} + CaCl_{2} + 2H_{2}O}$
Uses: bleaching cotton, linen and wood pulp; disinfecting drinking water; as an oxidising agent in industry.

questions.question:
(a) Explain the importance of pH in the human digestive system.

(b) Explain how a change of pH causes tooth decay.
answer_steps: (a) The stomach makes hydrochloric acid for digestion. Too much acid causes pain and irritation (indigestion); an antacid such as milk of magnesia neutralises the extra acid.
(b) Bacteria in the mouth make acids from sugar and food left after eating. When the pH falls below 5.5, tooth enamel (calcium hydroxyapatite) starts to corrode.
Brushing with basic toothpaste neutralises the acid and prevents decay.

questions.question: How is plaster of Paris formed? Write an equation to show the reaction between plaster of Paris and water. Write the uses of plaster of Paris.
answer_steps: Gypsum is heated at 373 K: $\mathrm{CaSO_{4} \cdot 2H_{2}O \xrightarrow{373\,K} CaSO_{4} \cdot \tfrac{1}{2}H_{2}O + 1\tfrac{1}{2}H_{2}O}$
With water: $\mathrm{CaSO_{4} \cdot \tfrac{1}{2}H_{2}O + 1\tfrac{1}{2}H_{2}O \rightarrow CaSO_{4} \cdot 2H_{2}O}$
Uses: plaster for supporting fractured bones, making toys and decorative materials, and making surfaces smooth.

questions.question: Blue litmus paper is dipped in a solution and turns red. The solution may be:
questions.explanation: Vinegar contains acetic acid; acids turn blue litmus red.

questions.question: Which gas is evolved when sodium hydrogencarbonate reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid?
questions.explanation: $\mathrm{NaHCO_{3}(s) + HCl(aq) \rightarrow NaCl(aq) + H_{2}O(l) + CO_{2}(g)}$
option_feedback: Hydrogen comes from metals with acids.

questions.question: The pH of gastric juice is about:
questions.explanation: Gastric juice contains hydrochloric acid and is strongly acidic.

questions.question: Tooth decay starts when the pH of the mouth falls below:
questions.explanation: Below pH 5.5, acids start to corrode tooth enamel.

questions.question: The chemical formula of baking soda is:
questions.explanation: Baking soda is sodium hydrogencarbonate.
option_feedback: That is sodium carbonate (washing soda without water).

questions.question: In the chlor-alkali process, the gas formed at the anode is:
questions.explanation: Chlorine forms at the anode and hydrogen at the cathode.
option_feedback: Chloride ions are discharged, not oxygen.
There is no carbon in brine.

questions.question: Which salt gives a solution with pH more than 7?
questions.explanation: Sodium carbonate comes from a weak acid and a strong base, so its solution is basic.

questions.question: A bee sting injects methanoic acid. The best first aid is to rub:
questions.explanation: Baking soda is a mild base that neutralises the acid.
option_feedback: Salt is neutral and does not neutralise the acid.
Vinegar is an acid; it adds to the sting.

questions.question: Number of water molecules in one formula unit of gypsum:
questions.explanation: Gypsum is CaSO₄·2H₂O; plaster of Paris has half a molecule; copper sulphate has 5; washing soda has 10.

questions.question: Which oxide will turn red litmus blue when dissolved in water?
questions.explanation: Calcium oxide is a metal oxide, so it is basic.

**Assertion (A):** A solution of pH 2 is more acidic than one of pH 5.

**Reason (R):** The lower the pH, the lower the concentration of hydrogen ions.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.

questions.question:
**Assertion (A):** Plaster of Paris is stored in moisture-proof containers.

**Reason (R):** Plaster of Paris sets into gypsum when it absorbs water.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Moisture would turn it into hard gypsum: R explains A.
option_feedback: Correct! A is true: moisture would make it set into hard gypsum. R is true: this setting reaction is exactly why it is kept dry.
R does explain A: this setting reaction is exactly why it is kept dry.
Check the Reason again: it is true, because this setting reaction is exactly why it is kept dry.
Check the Assertion again: it is true, because moisture would make it set into hard gypsum.

questions.question:
**Assertion (A):** Water should be added to a concentrated acid for dilution.

**Reason (R):** Dilution of a concentrated acid is highly exothermic.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.

**Assertion (A):** Washing soda is used to remove the permanent hardness of water.

**Reason (R):** Baking soda is used in fire extinguishers.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.

questions.question: What is water of crystallisation? Give an example.
answer_steps: It is the fixed number of water molecules present in one formula unit of a salt crystal.
Example: copper sulphate, CuSO₄·5H₂O, has five; on heating, $\mathrm{CuSO_{4} \cdot 5H_{2}O \xrightarrow{\Delta} CuSO_{4} + 5H_{2}O}$

questions.question: Why does lime water turn milky when carbon dioxide is passed through it, and why does the milkiness disappear when excess gas is passed?
answer_steps: Insoluble calcium carbonate forms: $\mathrm{Ca(OH)_{2}(aq) + CO_{2}(g) \rightarrow CaCO_{3}(s) + H_{2}O(l)}$
With excess carbon dioxide, soluble calcium hydrogencarbonate forms: $\mathrm{CaCO_{3}(s) + H_{2}O(l) + CO_{2}(g) \rightarrow Ca(HCO_{3})_{2}(aq)}$

questions.question: Starting from common salt, how are (i) sodium hydroxide, (ii) baking soda and (iii) washing soda obtained? Write one equation for each.
answer_steps: (i) Electrolysis of brine: $\mathrm{2NaCl(aq) + 2H_{2}O(l) \rightarrow 2NaOH(aq) + Cl_{2}(g) + H_{2}(g)}$
(ii) $\mathrm{NaCl + H_{2}O + CO_{2} + NH_{3} \rightarrow NH_{4}Cl + NaHCO_{3}}$
(iii) Heat baking soda: $\mathrm{2NaHCO_{3} \xrightarrow{\Delta} Na_{2}CO_{3} + H_{2}O + CO_{2}}$, then recrystallise: $\mathrm{Na_{2}CO_{3} + 10H_{2}O \rightarrow Na_{2}CO_{3} \cdot 10H_{2}O}$

questions.question: Explain why metal oxides are called basic oxides and non-metal oxides are called acidic oxides, with one equation each.
answer_steps: Metal oxides react with acids to give a salt and water, like bases: $\mathrm{CuO + 2HCl \rightarrow CuCl_{2} + H_{2}O}$
Non-metal oxides react with bases to give a salt and water, like acids: $\mathrm{Ca(OH)_{2}(aq) + CO_{2}(g) \rightarrow CaCO_{3}(s) + H_{2}O(l)}$
So metal oxides are basic and non-metal oxides are acidic.

questions.question: What is the pH scale? Explain the importance of pH in (i) our digestive system (ii) tooth decay (iii) agriculture (iv) self-defence by animals and plants.
answer_steps: The pH scale (0 to 14) measures the hydrogen ion concentration: 7 is neutral, below 7 acidic, above 7 basic.
(i) Extra stomach acid causes indigestion; an antacid such as milk of magnesia neutralises it.
(ii) Tooth enamel corrodes below pH 5.5; brushing with basic toothpaste neutralises the acids.
(iii) Plants need a suitable pH; acidic soil is treated with lime or chalk.
(iv) Bee stings and nettle leaves inject methanoic acid; a base such as baking soda, or the dock leaf, relieves the pain.

questions.question: Describe how acids react with (i) metals (ii) metal carbonates (iii) metal oxides (iv) bases, giving a balanced equation for each. How would you test the gas in (i)?
answer_steps: (i) $\mathrm{Zn(s) + H_{2}SO_{4}(aq) \rightarrow ZnSO_{4}(aq) + H_{2}(g)}$
(ii) $\mathrm{Na_{2}CO_{3}(s) + 2HCl(aq) \rightarrow 2NaCl(aq) + H_{2}O(l) + CO_{2}(g)}$
(iii) $\mathrm{CuO + 2HCl \rightarrow CuCl_{2} + H_{2}O}$
(iv) $\mathrm{NaOH(aq) + HCl(aq) \rightarrow NaCl(aq) + H_{2}O(l)}$
The hydrogen in (i) burns with a pop sound near a burning candle.

questions.question:
Meera tested five liquids with a universal indicator: lemon juice (pH 2.2), pure water (7), soap solution (10), vinegar (3) and milk of magnesia (10.5).

(i) Which liquid is neutral? (1)

(ii) Which two liquids are basic? (1)

(iii) Arrange lemon juice, vinegar and pure water in increasing order of hydrogen ion concentration. OR Which liquid would you use to relieve acidity in the stomach, and why? (2)
answer_steps: (i) Pure water.
(ii) Soap solution and milk of magnesia.
(iii) Pure water < vinegar < lemon juice (lower pH means more H⁺ ions). OR Milk of magnesia: it is a mild base that neutralises the extra acid.

questions.question:
A doctor puts a white plaster on Ravi's fractured arm. At home, his mother uses washing soda to clean clothes and baking soda to make dhokla soft.

(i) What is the chemical formula of the substance used for the plaster? (1)

(ii) Why does baking soda make dhokla soft and spongy? (1)

(iii) How is washing soda prepared from baking soda? Write the equations. OR Why must the plaster powder be stored in an airtight container? Write the equation. (2)
answer_steps: (i) Plaster of Paris, $\mathrm{CaSO_{4} \cdot \tfrac{1}{2}H_{2}O}$.
(ii) On heating or with an acid it gives carbon dioxide, whose bubbles make the batter rise.

(iii) $\mathrm{2NaHCO_{3} \xrightarrow{\Delta} Na_{2}CO_{3} + H_{2}O + CO_{2}}$, then $\mathrm{Na_{2}CO_{3} + 10H_{2}O \rightarrow Na_{2}CO_{3} \cdot 10H_{2}O}$. OR It absorbs moisture and sets into gypsum: $\mathrm{CaSO_{4} \cdot \tfrac{1}{2}H_{2}O + 1\tfrac{1}{2}H_{2}O \rightarrow CaSO_{4} \cdot 2H_{2}O}$
